bioBn:
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram: a professional biography
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is well known for notable achievements in sport, as an army officer and in political leadership. His long career, from becoming a professional footballer in the 1960s to becoming Speaker of Parliament in 2026, is a unique example of steadfast commitment, determination and public service.

Early life and education
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad was born on 29 October 1944 into a respected Bengali Muslim family in Lalmohan, Bhola district. His father, Dr Azhar Uddin, was an influential political figure and a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan. His mother, Mosammat Karimun Nesa, was a homemaker. In 1965 he obtained a master's degree (MA) in political science from the University of Dhaka, which laid the foundation for his later political life.

Contribution and success in sport
Before beginning his military and political life, he won particular fame as a footballer and was recognised as one of the most talented players of his time. A dynamic forward, he played for several leading clubs, including Mohammedan Sporting Club. He represented the Pakistan national football team from 1967 until Bangladesh gained independence in 1971. Internationally, he played matches in Iran, Turkey and Myanmar. Between 1964 and 1966 he set records in the 100 metres and 200 metres sprints in what was then East Pakistan. His extraordinary speed and competitive sporting skill took him to a distinguished position in South Asian football. In recognition of his contribution to football, FIFA awarded him its Centennial Order of Merit in 2005, one of the most prestigious honours in world sport.

Military contribution to Bangladesh's War of Independence
In Bangladesh's War of Independence in 1971, Hafiz Uddin Ahmad showed deep patriotism. A commissioned officer in the Pakistan Army, he took an active part in frontline combat while a captain in various strategically important sectors, especially in Sector 8 and under Z Force. On 30 March 1971, as an officer of the East Bengal Regiment, he declared a revolt against the Pakistan government at Jashore Cantonment. He then fought the Pakistani army for about eight hours and came out of the cantonment with two hundred soldiers. For his outstanding bravery and tactical skill he was awarded the Bir Bikram, Bangladesh's third-highest military award, which established him as a distinguished freedom fighter. His great sacrifice played a major role in the country's winning of independence. On 15 December 1971, after a day-long battle under Z Force, led by the then Major Ziaur Rahman, he captured Sylhet town.

Political life
Mr Hafiz was first elected MP for the Bhola-3 parliamentary constituency in 1986, and later, in 1992, he joined the BNP. In his parliamentary career he was elected MP to the 3rd (1986), 4th (1988), 5th (1991), 6th (1996), 7th (1996), 8th (2001) and 13th (2026) Parliaments. In his political life he took on party posts in the BNP and joined its standing committee, a reflection of his special standing in the party. He was later elected a member of the "National Standing Committee", the BNP's highest policymaking forum.
As a minister he has successfully held several important portfolios, including State Minister for Commerce (1996); Minister of Water Resources, Minister of Commerce and Minister of Jute (2001-2006); and, most recently, Minister of Liberation War Affairs (2026).
In March 2026 he was unanimously elected Speaker of the 13th Parliament of Bangladesh, and the Honourable President administered his oath. As Speaker of Parliament he presides over the sessions of Parliament in conducting parliamentary business, and continues to provide leadership at an important juncture in Bangladesh's democratic development.

Personal life and ideology
The distinguished educationist Dilara Hafiz was the wife of Hafiz Uddin Ahmad. Dilara Hafiz served as principal of Eden Mohila College, Dhaka, and of Shaheed Suhrawardy College, and as director general (DG) of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education. Dilara Hafiz died on 28 March 2026.
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is the father of two sons and one daughter. His son Shahrukh Hafiz is a computer engineer by profession and his son Taharat Hafiz is a businessman, and his daughter Shamama Shahrin Hafiz has completed an MBA at the University of Windsor in Canada. He is universally recognised for his discipline in his personal and sporting life, his military orderliness, his political experience and his integrity.
He is a devoted supporter of the core spirit of the War of Independence and has always spoken out for a strong democracy, institutional accountability, national development and the rule of law. His clear positions and candid views on contemporary issues have established him as a principled politician.

Achievements
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad's working life is a vast canvas of success in many fields: he is at once a FIFA-recognised footballer, a freedom fighter decorated with the Bir Bikram, a decorated military officer, a seven-time elected member of parliament and an experienced minister. Now serving as Speaker of Parliament, he has a career of more than six decades that reflects his commitment to national progress and shows a unique union of personal excellence and public service in Bangladesh's democratic evolution.
summaryBn: Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram is a Bangladeshi politician and freedom fighter who was awarded the title of Bir Bikram for his heroic contribution to the Liberation War of 1971. He currently serves as Speaker of the 13th Parliament of Bangladesh.
leadBn: Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram is a Bangladesh Nationalist Party member of the 13th Parliament elected from Bhola-3.
